description.narrative: (Maldives): Following 30 years of authoritarian rule, Maldives held its first multi-party elections in 2008. Reforming and building institutions and consolidating democratic norms have been challenges in Maldives. In addition, Maldives is attempting to transition from a highly centralized government to one in which local island councils have a more meaningful role in the political sphere.Through the Strong and Inclusive Maldivian Democracy activity, USAID will use FY 2022 funds to strengthen the capacity of key national and local democratic institutions by providing assistance to the government to implement decentralization and justice sector reforms. In addition, USAID will build the capacity of civil society and media to engage in effective advocacy and oversight. To build a sustainable foundation for a strong and inclusive democracy, this activity will also support civic education and better connect Maldivian citizens with their government.Through this activity, USAID will work closely with government counterparts, including the President's Office and the Local Government Authority, to build the capacity of local councils and women's development committees to engage in participatory and inclusive development processes. USAID will partner with key institutions in the justice sector, including the Judicial Services Commission, the Maldives Judicial Academy, and the Maldives Bar Council, to increase the quality of justice administration and professionalism of legal practitioners. In turn, justice sector support will increase access to justice for marginalized communities.The activity advances Integrated Country Strategy Mission Goal 3: Supported the development of a resilient, diverse, and inclusive Maldivian democracy..
